correctness.rationale: The stationary three-state Fourier resolvent is derived from the generator including the reset injection; a direct quadratic sign test yields 0<lambda_-<(r+beta)/v<lambda_+, and the slow residue is strictly positive for both preparations. Explicit first-order ballistic equations give the conditional ratio. The implicit equation F(R,z)=0 has negative F_z on its physical branch; stationary conditions reduce to an intersection of a strictly decreasing and a strictly increasing function with exactly one crossing, and both endpoint polarization limits vanish. This is an analytic proof for every positive parameter choice. 363 reproducible symbolic/numerical assertions independently check polynomial manipulations, resolvent inversion and optimization.

value.rationale: Conditioning on rare large displacements asks whether distant relocations overwhelmingly move outward, a physically measurable directional-selection quantity not determined by a scalar stationary position density. Resetting can suppress or enhance the conditional outward bias; the strict single maximizing reset frequency gives a natural control law for every positive switching/diffusion parameter set, with both small/large reset limits and a benchmark. This is distinct from already known mean-first-arrival rate optimization and not a narrow arbitrary parameter slice.
